claims.text: The untreated material is a predominantly single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy with limited room-temperature ductility.
The untreated RHEA has high strength and high-temperature stability.
A controlled aging treatment followed by rapid quenching can induce uniformly dispersed, coherent dual or hierarchical nanoscale precipitates in the BCC RHEA.
Nanoprecipitation can improve the strength–ductility synergy of multi-principal-element alloys.
Dual- or multiphase design can improve strength–ductility synergy relative to a single-phase alloy.
The proposed coherent nanoprecipitates will mediate multistage strain hardening.
The proposed nanoprecipitate dispersion will delay localized plastic instability.
Coherent nanoprecipitates obstruct dislocation motion and thereby produce progressive strain hardening.
Progressive strain hardening caused by the precipitates will increase room-temperature ductility and uniform deformation.
Fine, coherent precipitates will not introduce critical defects that reduce the alloy's high strength.
The aging treatment and precipitates will not alter the alloy's reactive composition.
Preserving the reactive composition will preserve impact-induced energy release.
The aged alloy will have greater room-temperature strain to failure and more uniform deformation than the untreated alloy.
The aged alloy will retain the untreated alloy's yield and ultimate strength.
The aged alloy will retain impact-induced combustion energy release comparable to the untreated alloy.
Excessive precipitate growth or coarsening can cause intermetallic embrittlement.
The hypothesis applies only to compositions that support coherent precipitation without unwanted grain-boundary phase formation.
A decisive test compares untreated and aged samples using microscopy, room-temperature mechanical testing, and dynamic impact energy-release measurements.

Failure to achieve a statistically significant improvement, exemplified by at least 50% greater strain before failure, while maintaining strength and comparable energy release falsifies the hypothesis.
